What Injuries Are Often Connected to Dog Attacks?

Dogs attack using their teeth and claws. This leads to many types of skin and soft-tissue injuries, along with potential crush injuries from the pressure of a dog’s jaw. In addition, a victim can suffer injuries from a fall if a dog jumps up and pushes the victim down. Common injuries include:
Cuts and scrapes
Deeper lacerations
Puncture wounds
Bruising or contusions
Bone fractures
Evisceration
Degloving
Facial injuries
Head and scalp injuries
Permanent scarring or disfigurement
Infections
Rabies and other diseases

In a severe dog attack, a dangerous or aggressive dog may go for the kill. This means the dog may target vulnerable areas of the victim’s body, such as the face and neck. Sadly, some dogs cause fatal injuries. If you have any type of injury or a loved one passed away from injuries caused by a dog attack in Thornton, our lawyers are here to help.
How Does Colorado’s Dog Bite Law Work?

Colorado Revised Statutes Section 13-21-124 contains the state’s dog bite law. It permits a person who “suffers serious bodily injury or death from being bitten by a dog while lawfully on public or private property” to bring a lawsuit against the dog owner to recover economic damages. These refer to the financial, tangible and specific losses that the victim suffered because of the dog bite, such as medical bills and lost wages.

Furthermore, it states that a civil lawsuit can be brought against a dog owner for a bite injury “regardless of the viciousness or dangerous propensities of the dog or the dog owner’s knowledge of these propensities or lack thereof.” In other words, a dog owner in Colorado will be financially responsible for the actions of his or her pet, whether or not the owner was negligent in failing to prevent a foreseeable dog attack.
Strict Liability vs. One-Bite Laws

Colorado’s dog bite law is a strict liability law, meaning it is not necessary to prove the pet owner’s negligence to hold him or her responsible for a bite injury. Many other states use a one-bite rule, which requires a plaintiff to provide evidence that a pet owner knew or reasonably should have known about a dog’s vicious propensities and failed to prevent an attack. Colorado’s strict liability law makes it easier for a victim to hold a dog owner accountable for a bite injury.

However, a pet owner in Thornton may try to avoid liability by alleging that you were trespassing or provoked the dog at the time of the attack. A dog owner in Colorado can also avoid liability for bodily injuries caused by a dog if he or she had clear and conspicuous signs on the property stating, “No Trespassing” or “Beware of Dog.” You or your attorney may have to combat these defenses to secure fair financial compensation for your claim.
What to Do After a Dog Bite Injury (How to Report a Dog Bite in Thornton)
If you get bitten by a dog in Thornton, do your best to stay calm and remember to take the following steps to protect yourself:
If it is an emergency, call 911 to report the dog attack and request an ambulance.
Exchange information with the pet owner, including finding out if the dog is up to date on its vaccinations.
Take photographs of the location of the attack, if you can.
Get immediate medical attention. Dog bite injuries often require wound debridement, cleaning and antibiotics to prevent infection.
Contact the City of Thornton Animal Control to report the incident. It is important for the city to keep track of dog bite incidents for the record.
Keep copies of all of your medical bills, income statements, photographs and other evidence that may support your claim.
Contact a Thornton dog bite injury lawyer for legal assistance as soon as possible.
Follow your doctor’s orders and work with your attorney to hold the pet owner legally responsible for an aggressive animal.
